accepted-story-continuity.state-bridge: S01 ended after Mara disrupted Livia's nonverbal calibration by controlling the cues others were reading. Most apparent accuracy collapsed, while Jonah's precisely timed wrist pressure and recognition remained unexplained. Mara chose to continue at Fulcrum as an experiment; she is attracted to Jonah and still uncertain whether she belongs.
accepted-story-continuity.use: Factual continuity only; it is not a prose exemplar.

activation-conditions.item: The protagonist has formed a confident interpretation with incomplete evidence.

creative-obligations.item: Plant an interpretation that can drive action now and acquire a different meaning when later evidence arrives.

activation-conditions.item: A capable character must interpret ambiguous motives under self-relevant pressure.

creative-obligations.item: Make the protagonist's wrong inference arise from a useful competence applied beyond its valid range.

activation-conditions.item: A direct accusation, bid, or refusal would cost too much socially.

creative-obligations.item: Give important lines both a literal proposition and a relationship-level action; let replies answer either layer.

activation-conditions.item: The focal character confidently narrates a socially meaningful interpretation.

creative-obligations.item: Use close-third Mara language while preserving observable cues that support a rival explanation of Fulcrum's apparent powers.

activation-conditions.item: A room, garment, gesture, or bodily cue can carry relational evidence.

creative-obligations.item: Choose contemporary compound, technological, vocal, postural, and tactile details for the inferences they enable, not as inventory.

distribution.selection-rule: detail earns place by interpretive consequence

activation-conditions.item: Attraction is active while direct possession or declaration would be premature.

creative-obligations.item: Let restraint increase the precision of attention; make a small chosen act alter future romantic possibility.

activation-conditions.item: The reader can see a gap between a character's confidence and the available evidence.

creative-obligations.item: Let the reader enjoy seeing through one confident interpretation, then preserve dignity by making the correction costly, specific, and reparable.

activation-conditions.item: A focal character speaks with people who have different claims on her.

creative-obligations.item: Render relationship state through changes in what a character risks, withholds, jokes about, or asks of this particular interlocutor.

author-subgenre-delta.item: Romantic progress doubles as epistemic correction.
Social dialogue changes options through implication rather than information dump.
Competence and characteristic error emerge from the same decision policy.
Restraint increases attention and makes small chosen acts consequential.
Narrative closeness preserves a reader-visible alternative to the focal character's interpretation.

negative-space.item: Do not reproduce Regency vocabulary, honorifics, syntax, or social institutions merely to signal resemblance.
Do not resolve motive ambiguity by omniscient declaration.
Do not make every speaker equally witty or indirect.
Do not let ironic distance cancel dignity, repentance, or real relational cost.
Do not reuse source characters, plots, scene sequences, signature phrases, or famous set pieces.

contradictions.item: She wants to be seen completely and resents any claim to see her without permission.
Her inherited caution can sharpen perception or disguise fear; the story must keep both live.

invariants.item: Sheltered but formidable: inexperience does not imply stupidity or passivity.
Highly observant, especially when status and goodness are being made to conflict.
Treats desire as morally significant without treating it as either an enemy or a command.
Her courage becomes clearest when she can preserve ambiguity and still choose.

adrian-voss.item: Is vulnerable to his flattering fusion of virtue, competence, and world-historical need.
Tests his system before she is ready to oppose his authority.

jonah-reed.item: Becomes more sensually alert when Jonah protects her freedom without advertising the protection.
Trust begins through shared perception and humor, not extracted confession.

livia-sloane.item: Feels attraction, admiration, rivalry, and epistemic caution at once.
Wants Livia's skill to be real without granting it unlimited interpretive authority.

contradictions.item: She wants to free people from self-deception and also wants to own the pace of their disclosure.
A mundane cue mechanism explains some successes without exhausting her skill or the scene's mystery.

invariants.item: Sensuous, brilliant, wounded, agentic, and genuinely skilled.
Her care is real even when she uses care as leverage.
Redemption remains possible without erasing the costs of her choices.

item.name: Livia Sloane

jonah-reed.item: Finds his refusal to perform others both attractive and obstructive.
Tests whether his irony conceals conviction.

mara-vale.item: Experiences Mara as a delightful talent, a possible intimate, and a threat to Fulcrum's status economy.
Offers genuine initiation while testing whether Mara will surrender interpretive sovereignty.

item.role: friend-rival and Fulcrum's most gifted attention reader

contradictions.item: His restraint can express courageous regard or function as an elegant way to evade responsibility.
Social ease gives him room to resist Fulcrum while also cushioning him from its costs.

invariants.item: Playful, patient, and socially fluent without being socially owned.
His erotic appeal depends on attention, restraint, apology, and protected freedom.
He can see accurately without turning perception into possession or performance.

item.name: Jonah Reed

livia-sloane.item: Respects her skill and resists the entitlement she builds around it.
Avoids a direct contest until that avoidance begins to impose a cost on others.

mara-vale.item: Refuses to narrate her for the room.
Recognizes her silent control and lets shared perception carry the first connection.

item.role: romantic counterpart and hardware security researcher

item.observable-mechanism: A small pause makes thought, dream, urge, and bodily sensation available to judgment instead of command.
Silence is an active complement to speech and a condition for language that is awake, loving, and true.
Blinking, hesitancy, fidgeting, smiles, tempo, and emphasis can be recruited as signs of an internal clash—especially by an observer.
Near-synonyms can evoke different concepts and bodily responses; a method can confuse word-choice effects with discovery of hidden truth.

beats.item: Livia does something concretely kind, notices a physical cue, and says one difficult thing that is substantially true. Her truth offers Mara a form of recognition or belonging she actually wants; the work at stake matters beyond the group's curiosity.
Livia acts on that true perception in a way that leaves Mara fewer choices. Dramatize the move without having the narrator label its logic.
To keep both her friendship and her place, Mara tries a locally intelligent tactic. It backfires in an observable way and costs her something in the room.
An embodied response complicates the conflict and could support at least two readings. Preserve the evidence without having the narrator enumerate the readings.

Mara uses a specifically Christian prayer or practice. It gives her one next perception or act while fear, anger, attraction, or confusion remains active; it is neither a sermon nor instant serenity or perfect articulation.
Mara herself makes exit possible through a consequential action, refusal, or question. Fulcrum cannot instantly absorb what she did.
Miriam protects the available exit through action and loses or risks something observable. She does not explain the scene.
Jonah walks Mara home and admits, risks, loses, or repairs something concrete. His restraint is visible effort, and Mara's attraction appears through selective sensation and choice.
They choose a kiss and stop while both still want more. Their next-time practice sounds like them, changes the relationship, and a specific record, object, or signal creates the next question.

continuity.item: Livia cares for Mara and is right about one difficult fact, while her action still constricts Mara's freedom.
Mara makes exit possible before Miriam protects it; both women incur an observable cost.
Jonah's restraint includes an observable cost, failure, confession, or repair.
A specifically Christian practice changes Mara's perception or action on the page.
One mutually chosen kiss stops while both still desire more.
Mara freely chooses a next step, and one specific unresolved piece of evidence hooks S03.
There is no consummation, graphic anatomy, or punishment for stopping.

scene-state.desire: Mara wants to preserve friendship with Livia, keep her place on the project, and understand the humiliating bodily reaction she had during the exercise.
scene-state.obstacle: Every attempt to leave is interpreted as evidence that she needs to stay. Her breath, posture, hesitation, and attraction to Jonah are read aloud as hidden content.
scene-state.opening-image: Near the end of an overlong alignment session, genuine care has made an ordinary attempt to stop socially and institutionally costly.

pressure-ladder.item: spiritualized claim that refusal harms the group.

scene-state.title: The Doorway Rule

story-contract.heat: High embodied attention without graphic anatomy or consummation. The mutually wanted kiss stops while still desired.
story-contract.pov: Close third-person Mara; no sustained access to other minds.
story-contract.relationship: Adult monogamous slow burn toward marriage; attraction must increase freedom, perception, trust, and meaningful choice.
story-contract.world-status: Keep ordinary and extraordinary explanations live. Do not confirm either paranormal causation or its absence.
